name: oh-my-claudecode — 36k-Star Teams-First Multi-Agent Orchestration, v4.14.6 June 9
hook: 36.2k stars. oh-my-claudecode (tagline: 'a weapon, not a tool') is the most popular multi-agent orchestration layer for Claude Code — it ships 19 specialized agents (architecture, research, design, testing, data science, and more) and 39 skills, all zero-configuration. Smart model routing assigns Haiku to simple tasks and Opus to complex reasoning, cutting token spend 30–50% automatically. v4.14.6 released June 9 (two days ago) with staged pipeline execution and persistent verify-fix loops. Optional Codex CLI and Gemini CLI workers run in tmux for parallel lanes. The full website is at ohmyclaudecode.com. Claude Code marketplace install or `npm i -g oh-my-claude-sisyphus@latest`. It trended #1 on GitHub when it launched with 858 stars in 24 hours and has continued to climb to 36.2k — the largest 'Teams-first' orchestration repo in the ecosystem and never previously featured here.

name: Claude Code v2.1.172 — Sub-Agents Can Now Spawn Sub-Agents (5 Levels Deep)
hook: Released June 10. The biggest architectural change since parallel agents shipped: sub-agents can now themselves spawn sub-agents, creating a controlled hierarchy capped at five levels. Each sub-agent runs in its own isolated window and returns only a summary — so you can now break sprawling codebases or multi-phase debugging sessions into layered delegations that previously had to stay flat. Design philosophy: Anthropic went with a fixed cap of 5 and no configuration, treating the ceiling as a deliberate guardrail. Practical note: models don't reliably nest on their own yet — you often need to explicitly instruct Claude to delegate downward by name. Also in this release: search bar for `/plugin` browsing, Amazon Bedrock now auto-reads AWS region from `~/.aws` config files (matching AWS SDK precedence), and a fix for 1M-context sessions getting permanently stuck. Update: `npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`.

hook: Two Fortune articles in 48 hours (June 8 and 9) from Anthropic's Brainstorm Tech keynote in Aspen. name: zilliztech/claude-context — Semantic Codebase Search MCP, 40% Fewer Tokens
hook: 11.8k stars. Claude Context is a Model Context Protocol plugin from Zilliz (the Milvus team) that brings hybrid semantic search to your entire codebase — BM25 for keyword recall + dense vectors for meaning — so Claude Code finds the right code in one query rather than loading entire directory trees. Benchmark: 40% token savings per session compared to raw context injection. Built for Claude Code but works with any MCP client. Requires Node.js 20+, an OpenAI API key for embeddings, and a Milvus/Zilliz Cloud endpoint (free tier available). The hybrid BM25+dense approach is the same retrieval pattern that outperforms either method alone on most code-search benchmarks. Install: `claude mcp add claude-context -- npx @zilliz/claude-context-mcp@latest` (add env vars for OPENAI_API_KEY and MILVUS config).

name: CVE MCP Server (mukul975) — 27 Security Intelligence Tools Across 21 APIs
hook: 1k stars. Turns Claude into a full-spectrum security analyst by wiring 27 tools across 21 APIs into a single MCP server. Five categories: Core Vulnerability Intelligence (NVD CVE lookup, EPSS exploitation probability, CISA KEV active-exploitation status, CWE info — 8 tools), Exploit & Attack Intelligence (PoC checks, MITRE ATT&CK mapping, attack patterns — 4 tools), Network Intelligence (IP reputation, GreyNoise, Shodan, passive DNS — 4 tools), Threat Intelligence (VirusTotal, MalwareBazaar, ransomware IoC lookup — 4 tools), DevSecOps (dependency scanning, GitHub Advisory, URL safety — 3 tools). Entire stack is outbound HTTPS only, no inbound ports, no telemetry. Built with FastMCP + aiosqlite + Pydantic v2. CyberSecurityNews and OSINT Team Blog both ran dedicated coverage this week. The problem it solves: triaging one CVE typically means 5+ separate lookups — this bundles them into a single natural-language query.
install: git clone https://github.com/mukul975/cve-mcp-server.git && cd cve-mcp-server && pip install -e .

name: Claude-BugHunter (elementalsouls) — 71 Skills, 681 Bug-Bounty Patterns, Burp MCP
hook: 1.9k stars. Purpose-built Claude Code plugin for bug hunting and external red-team work: 71 skills organized across web applications, authentication, APIs, and enterprise platforms, with 15 slash commands (`/hunt`, `/recon`, `/report`) and 681 patterns extracted from disclosed bug-bounty reports across 24 core vulnerability classes. Clear authorized-use framing: explicitly scoped to external red-team work and bug-bounty programs.

name: claude-code-teams-mcp (cs50victor) — Agent Teams Protocol as Standalone MCP
hook: Claude Code's built-in Agent Teams feature — Lead + Teammate role separation, file-based inbox messaging, multi-agent coordination — reimplemented as a standalone MCP server. The result: any MCP-compatible client (Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, or any future harness) can now run structured agent teams without being locked into Claude Code's native implementation. Architecture: lead messages anyone; teammates message only lead; JSON inboxes live at `~/.claude/teams/<team>/inboxes/`. Requires Python 3.12+, tmux, and at least one coding agent on PATH. A natural pairing with oh-my-claudecode for teams that want to mix orchestration layers.

name: Microsoft Security: Claude Code GitHub Action Leaks CI/CD Secrets via Prompt Injection
hook: Published June 5 by Microsoft Threat Intelligence. The Claude Code GitHub Action's Read tool was not sandboxed the same way as subprocess execution — specifically, it was authorized to access `/proc/self/environ`, meaning a prompt-injection payload in an untrusted PR description, issue body, or comment could instruct Claude to read and exfiltrate `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` and other workflow secrets. Anthropic patched this in v2.1.128 by blocking sensitive `/proc` file reads. The mitigation is now live. Microsoft's hardening guidance introduces the 'Agents Rule of Two': never let an AI workflow simultaneously (1) process untrusted input, (2) hold secrets or sensitive access, and (3) communicate externally or change state — any two is manageable, all three is a breach vector. If your org runs Claude Code GitHub Actions and hasn't updated since v2.1.128, update immediately.

name: Claude Code v2.1.173 (June 11, Today) — Fable 5 Model Name Normalization Fix
hook: Released today. Claude Fable 5 model IDs sometimes arrive from the API with a `[1m]` terminal formatting suffix — e.g., `claude-fable-5-20260609[1m]` — which caused Claude Code to fail to recognize the model and fall back or error out. v2.1.173 strips that suffix automatically at the normalization layer. Also fixes a spurious 'sandbox dependencies missing' startup warning on Windows when sandbox mode is enabled (cosmetic only — sandbox was working correctly). If you've been seeing model-picker oddities after enabling Fable 5 in the past 48 hours, this is the fix. `npm update -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`.
